problem:
If $v=[\begin{aligned}a \\ b\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of 
$A=[\begin{aligned}3 & 5 \\ -2 & 1\end{aligned}]$
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda =2+3\text{i},$
then what is the value of $\frac{a}{b}?$

activity_context.topic_title: Finding Complex Eigenvectors of Real 2x2 Matrices

examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Complex Eigenvector of a Matrix Given a Complex Eigenvalue
examples.problem:
Find an eigenvector of 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14070616/assets/6e4a720878567b81cb593aa5a9bfc5aa2c8c7ace61d111bb8934bc94056c04bc.png)
that corresponds to the eigenvalue $\lambda=-3+4\textrm{i}.$
examples.worked_solution:
To compute the eigenvectors of a matrix, we need to find non-zero solutions of the matrix equation 

$$
(A - \lambda I) \textbf{x}=\mathbf{0}.
$$

 

In our case, we have $\,\lambda =-3+4\textrm{i},$ and

$$
\begin{aligned}A-\lambda I & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & 4 \\ -4 & -3\end{aligned}]-[\begin{aligned}-3+4\text{i} & 0 \\ 0 & -3+4\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}-4\text{i} & 4 \\ -4 & -4\text{i}\end{aligned}].\end{aligned}
$$

So, we have the homogeneous system of linear equations

$$
{\begin{aligned}-4\text{i}{x}_{1}+4{x}_{2}=0 \\ -4{x}_{1}-4\text{i}{x}_{2}=0.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since the matrix $A-(-3+4\textrm{i})I$ is singular, the system above must have a non-zero solution. This means that one equation of the system is a multiple of another.

As a result, we can drop one of the rows and take one of the variables to be the free variable. For example, from the second equation, we get

$$
x_1 = -\textrm{i}x_2.
$$

Therefore, the general solution is given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14070616/assets/0d2e7b9f7011624cf74762419efd784144cf41e2000301d093e1aa612e96f495.png)

Setting $x_2=1,$ we get the eigenvector ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14070616/assets/2e4bc467e9fbc15574d2739766eada3f297500ecf1a69382500271751b2edf65.png)

feedback.problem:
Determine whether $v=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2-2\text{i}\end{aligned}]$ is an eigenvector of the matrix $A=[\begin{aligned}-3 & -3 \\ 6 & 3\end{aligned}].$
If so, then what is the corresponding eigenvalue?
feedback.worked_solution:
The eigenvectors of $A$ are the non-zero vectors $v$ such that $Av=\lambda v.$ So, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}Av & =[\begin{aligned}-3 & -3 \\ 6 & 3\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6\text{i} \\ 6-6\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}6\text{i} \\ -6{\text{i}}^{2}-6\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =3\text{i}[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -2-2\text{i}\end{aligned}] \\  & =3\text{i}v.\end{aligned}
$$

Since $Av=3\text{i}v,$ we conclude that $v$ is an eigenvector of $A$ and the corresponding eigenvalue is $\lambda =3\text{i}.$
